topic: Conservation of Mechanical Energy and Heat-Work
key_concepts: Total mechanical energy is the sum of potential energy and kinetic energy
Potential energy is calculated as PE = mgh
Kinetic energy is calculated as KE = 1/2 mv²
In an ideal falling object, total mechanical energy remains constant
As height decreases, potential energy decreases and kinetic energy increases
At maximum height kinetic energy is zero; at ground level potential energy is zero
Real-life activities like kicking a ball, biking downhill, and riding a swing show energy
Adding heat to a system increases its internal energy
Heat can do work, such as steam spinning a pinwheel
Internal energy change equals heat added minus work done by the system
Work done on a system increases its internal energy
